title: The mutation figures recorded for the merchant-delist slice
note: Authored from the committed blob at the feature commit, before any replay ran. Each `find` was written by hand from the file as committed and each was counted exactly once before this manifest was saved; a replay that disagrees is a finding, not a number to adjust. `claimed_count` is deliberately absent from every entry: this is the FIRST recording, so there is no earlier measurement to re-check, and a hand-typed figure with nothing behind it is exactly the defect class this tool exists to catch. The four mutations are the slice's load-bearing pins: the catalogue exclusion (listing and detail), the checkout refusal, and the admin capability gate. The cart-add refusal has no mutation of its own because it shares the `is_active` read with the detail gate - breaking the field's readers is M2's shape - and its own pin (`test_cart_add_of_delisted_product_is_refused_as_not_found`) fails under a delist-field removal for the same reason the detail pin does.

mutations.description: the public listing serves delisted products: the base queryset drops the is_active filter, so a delisted row reappears in the catalogue and in every filtered/searched view of it

the public detail GET serves a delisted product: the 404 gate never fires, so the row is readable by slug and the endpoint becomes an oracle that distinguishes a delisted product from a nonexistent one
checkout silently skips a delisted cart line: the delist collection becomes a pass-through, the refusal never fires and the order is minted including a product that is not for sale

the delist action's capability gate is widened from products.publish to products.read, so the inventory role (which holds products.read but not publish) can take products off sale through a directly posted admin action
